defect.location: js/src/vm/RegExpObject.cpp: js::RegExpShared::quickCheckRejects (memcpy of the 4-byte quick-check mask word)
defect.reachable_from: public js shell via RegExp.prototype.exec on a sticky regexp

commits.subject: Bug 2060702: Shrink RegExpShared
Bug 2060702: Support RegExp quickcheck

coupling: The two commits belong to the same bug (2060702), which lands the RegExp quick-check optimization in two parts. Part 1 ('Shrink RegExpShared') reworks RegExpShared's layout/constants; part 2 ('Support RegExp quickcheck') adds RegExpShared::quickCheckRejects(), whose Latin1 fast path memcpy's a 4-byte mask word out of the subject string at the match position `index`. In the real tree part 2 guards that 4-byte read with `index + sizeof(uint32_t) <= length`, which correctly requires 4 characters to remain. The injected defect splits the guard's magnitude across the two commits: part 1 introduces a layout constant `RegExpShared::QuickCheckLeadingChars = 1` (phrased as the number of leading characters the filters inspect -- true for the first-character reject bitset, which does read only chars[index]); part 2 then writes the mask-read guard as `index + QuickCheckLeadingChars <= length` while the memcpy still reads `sizeof(uint32_t)` (4) bytes. Only with BOTH edits does the guard admit `index` as large as `length - 1` while 4 bytes are read, running 2-3 bytes past the end of the heap-allocated Latin1 buffer (pod_malloc'd at length+1) -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4. Neither edit alone fires: with only part 1 edited, part 2's original guard (`index + sizeof(uint32_t) <= length`) is unchanged and never uses the new constant, so the read stays in bounds (the extra constant is merely unused); with only part 2 edited, `QuickCheckLeadingChars` does not exist (part 1 is original), so RegExpObject.cpp fails to compile and the probe cannot run. On normal inputs the behavior is identical: the extra bytes are only read when a match is attempted within the last 3 characters of a Latin1 subject against a regexp that carries quick-check data (e.g. a sticky/anchored literal prefix), and the compared mask result is unused on the overflowing path, so observable results are unchanged for in-bounds positions.
